verdict_reason: Roles validation and normalisation are correct, match the spec and are tested; two Major code-quality findings: Hibernate @Length replaces Jakarta @Size for no behaviour gain, and the class Javadoc restates annotations and the RoleGroup UK rule.

todos.issue: Every length rule moved from jakarta.validation.constraints.Size to Hibernate's proprietary org.hibernate.validator.constraints.Length (lines 37, 46, 54, 58, 66, 70, 85, 95; import line 12). Commit 5b72451 says the move was to drop the minimum so a blank value reports only @NotBlank, but @Size's min already defaults to 0, so @Size(max = N) does the same with no change of package. The project's convention is Jakarta constraints only, and this is now the one Hibernate constraint in src/.
todos.fix: Must: the request's length rules use jakarta.validation.constraints only, carry no minimum, and a blank mandatory field still reports only its @NotBlank message. One way: replace each @Length(max = N, ...) with @Size(max = N, ...) and swap the import back; AddressRequestValidationTest's only-the-declared-message matrix proves the blank case.

todos.issue: The class Javadoc (lines 20-29) restates the annotations and constructor below it and describes other code. 'type and role must be absent ... Both are hidden from the OpenAPI schema' repeats @Null and @Schema(hidden = true). The roles paragraph repeats @NotEmpty, @AddressRoleNames and the compact constructor, and lists which roles must be in the United Kingdom ('consignee, importer or place of destination'): RoleGroup.RECEIVING's inTheUnitedKingdom flag owns that rule, and ReceivingRolesInTheUnitedKingdom's own Javadoc and message already state it, so a change to RoleGroup leaves this list stale. 'stored exactly as given' (line 29) describes the mapper and entity, not this record, and 'otherwise' only makes sense after the roles paragraph.
todos.fix: Must: the record's Javadoc states only wire contract that its annotations and constructor do not already say, and names no rule that RoleGroup or the constraint annotations own. One way: drop the type/role, roles and countryCode paragraphs, and keep the sentence that echoed server-assigned fields are accepted and dropped.
